events.title: The Vibrant Symphony of a Mind by JJ Roach
events.description: April 2 to 30 • Regitz Gallery Opening reception: Friday, April 2, 2027 • 5-8 PM JJ Roach turns inner rhythm into art, with intricate pen-on-paper masterpieces that use thousands of precise lines to weave galaxies, patterns, and cosmic swirls. A 22-year-old autistic artist and lifelong resident of Lancaster, JJ’s work often reflects natural patterns—the Fibonacci sequence, fractals, and spirals found in shells, galaxies, and storms—drawn entirely by hand, dot by dot, spiral by spiral, with no digital tools, rulers, or preliminary sketches. Draw closer and discover superhuman detail that lingers long after the first encounter.

events.title: Is creating beauty enough? by Kristin Hill
events.description: March 5 to 26 • Regitz Gallery Opening reception: Friday, March 5, 2027 • 5-8 PM Is beauty an indulgence, or is it central to life? As a career aviation artist, Kristin Hill is drawn to the dominance of beauty in her paintings, intertwining the technical function of flight with its grace and form. In this collaborative exhibit, Hill explores the concept of beauty and its importance to the human spirit, while other artists investigate beauty in music, architecture, history, psychology, culture, our living environment, and beyond. About the Artist Kristin Hill is a nationally recognized aviation artist whose four-decade career has centered on fine-art oil painting, custom commissions, and the exploration of flight, sky, and landscape. Drawing on formal training in the fine arts, a lifelong connection to aviation, and firsthand experience flying in a wide range of aircraft—including a rare high-altitude U-2 flight with the U.S. Air Force—Hill brings both artistic sensitivity and technical precision to her work. Her paintings extend beyond aviation to encompass landscapes, skyscapes, still lifes, and the human figure, reflecting her ongoing interest in observation, atmosphere, and the visual experience of the world. Hill’s work has been exhibited internationally and is held in museum, corporate, private, and U.S. Air Force collections; she has also been an active participant in the U.S. Air Force Art Program since 1980 and a member of the American Society of Aviation Artists since 1987.

events.title: Kept Like a Secret by Kendyll Hillegas
events.description: February 5 to 26 • Regitz Gallery Opening reception: Friday, February 5, 2027 • 5-8 PM A glowing ear. Yellow leaves. An untethered kite. These images have persisted in Kendyll Hillegas’ awareness since childhood, like intermittent visual background noise. They appear without warning, often precipitating a cascade of emotion the artist calls The Feeling—a sudden longing, an acute awareness of time, an intense desire to know and be known. Through colorful oil paintings, Kept Like a Secret is Hillegas’ attempt to paint The Feeling by chasing the images that summon it, turning up the volume on the background noise and seeing where it leads. About the Artist Kendyll Hillegas is an award-winning illustrator and fine artist known for technical and emotional realism. Over the past decade, she has collaborated with clients including Coca-Cola, A24 Films, and Vanity Fair on a wide range of commercial and editorial projects. Her recent body of oil paintings expands on the precise, vivid realism she is known for as an illustrator, adding new layers of narrative complexity through landscape, large-scale portraits, and close-cropped figurative compositions. She exhibited her debut solo show “Kept Like a Secret” at The Gallery at St. Mary’s, Manhattan, in late 2025. She holds a BFA in Painting and works from her studio in York, Pennsylvania.

events.title: The Places We Go II by Ross Junior Owusu
events.description: December 4–January 29 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, December 4, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. The Places We Go II is a solo exhibition by Ghanaian mixed-media artist Ross Junior Owusu exploring migration as an interior and ongoing process of becoming. Through ceramics, assemblage, and mixed-media artwork, Owusu examines how memory, resilience, cultural identity, and belonging are carried, reshaped, and rebuilt across shifting landscapes. Using fragmented materials such as clay and reclaimed objects, Owusu presents migration not as a fixed journey of loss or arrival, but as a layered negotiation of selfhood. His sculptural works reflect the physical and emotional imprints of movement, exploring what is carried forward, what is left behind, and what endures. Clay serves as a central material and metaphor in Owusu’s practice, reflecting cycles of becoming, un-becoming, and re-becoming. His sculptural forms draw from West African visual languages, including textured surfaces and modular interpretations of Krobo bead structures, while referencing architecture, the human body, and emotional landscapes. Reclaimed bicycle parts and earthy surface treatments further evoke movement, resilience, transformation, and connection to place. Through repetition, assemblage, texture, and vibrant surface treatments, The Places We Go II invites viewers to consider how identity is continually shaped and reshaped by movement, memory, place, and relationships. The exhibition features approximately 10 works exploring the complex connections between cultural heritage and evolving environments. About the Artist Ross Junior Owusu is a Ghanaian mixed-media artist and educator working across ceramics, performance, and assemblage. He holds an MFA in Studio Art with a concentration in Ceramics from Wayne State University and a BA in Industrial Art with a concentration in Ceramics from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Ghana. He currently serves as an Assistant Professor of Art at Talladega College. Owusu’s artistic practice explores identity, migration, and cultural memory, examining how identities are carried, negotiated, and reassembled across changing geographies. His work combines contemporary mixed-media practices with West African visual languages, creating sculptural forms that connect inherited traditions with personal experience and contemporary environments.

events.title: Overshare: I Did This for Me by Shauna L Yorty
events.description: November 6–24 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, November 6, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. Overshare: I Did This for Me is a raw, intimate body of work by Lancaster-based artist Shauna L Yorty, created over three years of survival, transformation, and self-discovery. Through cardboard collages and mixed media artwork, including dimensional pieces, Yorty explores the messy, hopeful, and deeply personal process of making art as a means of moving through difficult experiences. Yorty describes the exhibition as a culmination of three years of “survival, process, and expression in service of love.” The works are made from humble, everyday materials and embrace an intentionally raw, handmade aesthetic. Bright colors, bold forms, layered textures, and dimensional elements transform discarded materials into expressive works of contemporary art. Rather than creating art for perfection or approval, Yorty makes art as a way to process, connect, and keep moving forward. Overshare: I Did This for Me invites viewers to consider their own stories, vulnerabilities, and creative processes, while finding connection with others through artistic expression. About the Artist Shauna L Yorty is a Lancaster-based artist whose bright, bold artwork tells powerful stories of hope and healing. Working from a systems-thinking perspective, Yorty draws connections between a lifetime of experiences, passions, and joys to create opportunities for people to connect with themselves, one another, and their own stories through the process of making art together. Yorty’s artistic practice centers on participation, storytelling, and connection. Their work encourages people to own, tell, and participate in their own stories, reflecting a belief in art as a tool for personal expression, healing, and community.

events.title: Heartland Marimba Festival – FREE
events.description: Make the Ware Center part of your Lancaster First Friday route! 7 p.m. • Lobby How did an instrument with roots in Africa find its way to the classical music stage—and what does Pennsylvania have to do with it? Join members of Heartland Marimba for a fascinating, hands-on exploration of the marimba’s sounds, science, and history. Discover how its distinctive acoustics work, trace its journey from Africa through Central America, and learn how U.S. companies and performers helped bring the instrument into classical music. You’ll also uncover some surprising local connections, including Clair Musser, the Manheim-born musician widely regarded as the “godfather” of classical marimba, and the Marimba Queens, an all-female ensemble based in Lancaster that toured the country for nearly 20 years, beginning in the 1930s. Whether you’re a music lover, history buff, or simply curious about this remarkable instrument, there’s something to discover! More First Friday fun: From 5–7 p.m., Millersville students will lead free, hands-on creative activities for kids in the lobby. Admission: FREE and open to the public! Accessibility: A touch tour will be available for blind and low-vision patrons. Please contact Barry Kornhauser for more information.

events.description: Tuesday, February 16, 2027 • 7 PM • Steinman Hall For years, artist Willie Baronet has collected signs from people experiencing homelessness, seeing in them not just a plea for help, but expressions of life, creativity, and humanity. In this moving film, he drives cross-country, “buying” signs and connecting with the people behind them. 6:15 PM • Pre-show community panel discussion Post-show • Q&A with director Willie Baronet

events.title: Disposable Humanity – FREE
events.description: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 • 7 PM • Steinman Hall A little-known chapter of Holocaust history. A story that demands to be remembered. In Disposable Humanity, the Mitchell family—esteemed Disability Studies scholars and filmmakers—examine the Nazi Aktion T4 program and its systematic murder of more than 300,000 disabled people. Targeted as having a “life unworthy of living,” these individuals became some of the Third Reich’s earliest victims of mass murder. Their deaths laid the groundwork for the Holocaust that followed. Join us for this investigative documentary and an opportunity to explore its historical significance through conversation with scholars, advocates, and community leaders. Admission: FREE • Tickets required 6:15 PM • Pre-show Community Panel Discussion Featuring: Dr. Emily Baldys, Chair of the MU Disability Film Festival Mr. Theo Braddy, Executive Director of the National Council on Independent Living Dr. Dennis Downey, Disability Scholar and MU History Professor Emeritus Dr. Stacey Irwin, Chair of the MU Holocaust & Genocide Conference Committee Mr. Bob Tortora, Member of the Word of Life Deaf Church Post-show • Q&A with director Cameron Mitchell Accessibility: The film is captioned. Live captioning (CART) and ASL interpreting will be provided for the panel discussion. Please contact Barry Kornhauser for more information. Co-presented by the MU Disability Film Festival and Congregation Shaarai Shomayim. Live captioning (CART) supported by the MU Office of Learning Services.

events.title: TAIKOPROJECT
events.description: Sunday, April 18, 2027 • 3 PM • Steinman Hall TAIKOPROJECT has astonished audiences worldwide since 2000 with their unique blend of traditional taiko & innovative aesthetics. Percussive power, dynamic music, and graceful choreography work together to weave a gorgeous narrative you’ll have to see (and hear) to believe! 2 PM • Lobby • Free kids’ activities and crafts! events.title: Jazz at Lincoln Center Presents World on a String: Swinging Songs of Broadway
events.description: Saturday, April 10, 2027 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Jazz at Lincoln Center returns as guest vocalists Kate Kortum and David Merino debut arrangements of tunes from Broadway’s most beloved productions—Hamilton, Wicked, South Pacific, West Side Story, and more—in a special concert event that musical theater fans and jazz lovers alike will adore Tickets: Adults $29 • Students: $21 Presented in partnership with Robert Bowman and Christine Kennedy.

events.title: Terrance Simien & The Zydeco Experience
events.description: Thursday, March 25, 2027 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Take a multicultural tour of the world with Grammy-winner Terrance Simien, inspired by the many countries he’s visited on tour. With accordion in hand, Simien creates a hypnotic blend of New Orleans funk-reggae-flavored world-blues-American zydeco roots music that beckons you to your feet and into the groove. Leading his Zydeco Experience band, Simien has become one of the most respected and accomplished artists in American roots music today. Tickets: Adults $27 • Students: $19

events.title: Cherish the Ladies
events.description: Wednesday, March 17, 2027 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Celebrate St. Patrick’s Day with Cherish the Ladies! Through 40 years of groundbreaking music, the group has captivated audiences worldwide as one of the most celebrated Irish ensembles in history. Renowned for their exhilarating blend of traditional Irish music, breathtaking vocals, and propulsive Irish step dancing, they have won the hearts of fans and critics alike. Tickets: Adults $35 • Students: $25

events.title: Milo the Magnificent
events.description: Saturday, February 27, 2027 • 3 PM • Steinman Hall A Jim Henson Foundation–grant-awarded production by Alex & Olmsted, Milo the Magnificent is a delightful and highly physical puppet play about an aspiring magician. This wordless comedy draws inspiration from turn-of-the-century vaudeville, showcasing stunningly innovative puppetry as Milo attempts a series of magic tricks—which don’t always go as planned. 2 PM • Lobby • Free kids’ activities and crafts! Tickets: Adults $15 • Students: $10

events.title: Electric Root: Let Love Lead, A Celebration of Black Music
events.description: Saturday, February 13, 2027 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Celebrate Valentine’s Day with an immersive, emotionally rich concert fueled by the musical traditions that have shaped our cultural soundscape. Led by acclaimed vocalists Brianna Thomas, C. Anthony Bryant, and Charenee Wade, Let Love Lead uplifts the contributions of Black musical excellence—including legends Donny Hathaway, Aretha Franklin, Nina Simone, and many more—illuminating its continued relevance in today’s world. Tickets: Adults $27 • Students: $19

events.title: Branford Marsalis and Dianne Reeves Celebrate John Coltrane
events.description: Thursday, February 4, 2027 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Grammy-winning jazz luminaries Branford Marsalis and Dianne Reeves join forces to celebrate the timeless ballads of John Coltrane. At the heart of the evening is the landmark 1963 recording by John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman, a masterwork of tenderness and restraint. Celebrate the enduring legacy of John Coltrane with some of the most intimate and emotionally transcendent jazz music ever recorded. Tickets: Adults $65 • Students: $55 Stay tuned for details about a VIP reception!

events.title: Tommy Dorsey Orchestra – Sentimental for the Season
events.description: Friday, December 18, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall In Big Band history, the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra is recognized as one of the best all-around dance bands—it could swing with the best of them, and no other band could come close to Tommy’s when it came to creating warm, sentimental ballads. Today’s one and only Tommy Dorsey Orchestra continues this great tradition. Experience explosive Big Band entertainment at its finest with this swinging show featuring holiday tunes and traditional favorites. Tickets: Adults $27 • Students: $19

events.title: The Hot Sardines – Holiday Stomp
events.description: Wednesday, December 9, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Jazz revivalists the Hot Sardines throw a raucous yuletide extravaganza inspired by classic holiday films (such as White Christmas and It’s a Wonderful Life) and timeless classics, with hat-tips to Louis Armstrong, Edith Piaf, Duke Ellington, and beyond. Get your season swinging with fresh takes on “Mistletoe and Holly,” “Le Noël de la Rue,” “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy,” “Blue Christmas,” “Christmas Blues,” “White Christmas,” “Please Come Home for Christmas,” and more. Tickets: Adults $35 • Students: $25

events.title: Seán Heely’s Celtic Christmas
events.description: Saturday, December 5, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Celebrate the season with U.S. National Scottish Fiddle Champion Seán Heely and a cast of nationally acclaimed performers in a festive journey through the Celtic world. Featuring stirring fiddle and bagpipes, dazzling Scottish and Irish dance, and a rich tapestry of Gaelic carols, traditional tunes, and familiar holiday favorites, this joyful production brings Winter Solstice traditions to life with energy and warmth. events.title: Layer The Walls: Turn of the Century
events.description: Saturday, November 21, 2026 • 3 PM • Steinman Hall In one Lower East Side tenement, forty layers of wallpaper were found clinging to the walls, each piece applied by a new immigrant family. Using puppetry, masks, and live action, Layer the Walls tells the incredible stories held within each layer—an Irish immigrant helping to build the Brooklyn Bridge, Italian brothers surviving the Great Blizzard of 1888, and two Russian Jewish garment workers joining the Uprising of 20,000 to fight for safety. Recommended for ages 8 and up. 2 PM • Lobby • Free kids’ activities and crafts! Tickets: Adults $15 • Students: $10 Accessibility: ASL interpretation, sensory-friendly accommodations, and audio description will be available. There will be a pre-show touch tour for blind and low-vision patrons. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more.

events.title: Flamenco y Sol: Flamenco at Its Essence
events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall An evening of traditional flamenco in its most authentic form, featuring live music, improvisation, and the dynamic interplay between dancer, singer, and guitarist. Rooted in the tablao tradition, the performance highlights the raw emotional power of flamenco, delivering an electrifying theatrical experience. Tickets: Adults $29 • Students: $21 6:30 PM • Pre-show flamenco lecture by Dr. Ana Börger-Greco Presented in partnership with the Skrodinsky Family Foundation.

events.title: Heartland Marimba Jukebox Night with Friends
events.description: Saturday, November 7, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Join the electrifying artists of Heartland Marimba and their fabulous guest performers as they fill the evening with the zippy and melodious sounds of marimbas and xylophones! Delight in music that spans decades, from modern pop inspirations to early 1900s ragtime and dance music, Argentine tango, and impressive grooves in between. Tickets: Adults $20 • Students: $15 Accessibility: Audio description will be available, and there will be a pre-show touch tour for blind and low-vision patrons. events.title: LBBB presents “Our Best Brass Christmas”
events.description: Sunday, December 20 • 3:00 PM • Steinman Hall Lancaster British Brass Band consists of 31 players. It draws its personnel from the four state regions of Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware and New Jersey. Originally conceived as a top-level, professional quality ensemble, it includes among its membership professional solo and ensemble players and music teacher/performers. The band members bring years of playing and teaching experience to the organization from such diverse institutions as The United States Marine Band, and the Lancaster, Harrisburg, Reading and York Symphony Orchestras. Many players are currently engaged as teachers in various public and private school venues and in such institutions of higher learning as West Chester, Millersville and Kutztown Universities, Lebanon Valley College, and The University of Delaware. Tickets: $25
